title: Concurrency-safe checkout allocation
summary: Atomic locking, tokenized leases and ownership-aware recovery protect concurrent engineering sessions and existing work.

dates.note: Exact project start/end dates remain unknown. Direct local source/history review on 2026-10-29 supplements the supplied October 5 snapshot and separately dated owner statements. Commit milestones and review dates are not project starts or release dates.

facts.text: Implemented concurrency-safe checkout allocation using project-wide atomic directory locks, tokenized refreshable leases and strict branch/cleanliness/remote checks before reuse.
Made reservations visible through untracked Git lease markers so normal cleanliness checks reject occupied checkouts; reclaimed only markers with proven allocator ownership.
Restricted failed-creation cleanup to allocator-owned partial state, preserving ambiguous markers and unexpected files.
The snapshot records 15 allocator test definitions using temporary repositories and simultaneous acquisitions in separate subprocesses; the analysis did not execute them.

Designed allocation as an ownership protocol with opaque lease tokens and paired checkout/session records: refresh and release require a matching token, while automatic expiry reclamation checks the marker's allocator metadata and untracked status before removal.

notes: Expiry reclamation can remove a recognized, expired allocator marker without the original holder supplying its token. It validates marker metadata and untracked status, but does not prove that the original engineering session has stopped. Matching-token requirements apply to explicit refresh/release operations.
